fields.expected: What draws me to humanoids is that they are the hardest version of a problem I keep running into: a learned system has to act in a world that does not forgive wrong actions. I built a Playwright-based job-application agent where a single bad click could submit a real application or fill a legal field incorrectly, so I designed it as a deterministic, operator-controlled agent with an explicit state machine and fail-closed flags like SUBMIT_ENABLED, plus a validation ladder that refused to call a capability working until it had been confirmed against live conditions rather than a local fixture. That is a software version of the problem manipulation has physically. I also built the ML core of an anomaly-detection system at Summer Atlantic Capital, including temporal sequence modeling over event streams and a learning-to-rank layer, and the thing that mattered most was not offline score but whether the output was operationally useful. Humanoid manipulation is where those two interests collide: models that have to generalize across messy contact-rich tasks, and evaluation that tells you honestly whether a policy will hold up outside the demo. I would rather work on that than on a benchmark.
